flashcards.q: What is the current stability status of the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (as of the version dated 2026-08-01)?
flashcards.a: Development status, not Stable, no 1.0 release. Main repo v1.42.0 (12 Jun 2026) moved all gen_ai.* content into a dedicated semantic-conventions-genai repository; attribute names can still change without a major version bump.

flashcards.q: What is the span naming pattern in the GenAI semantic conventions?
flashcards.a: {gen_ai.operation.name} {gen_ai.system}, e.g. a chat completion against Anthropic is named 'chat anthropic'.

flashcards.q: What are the three agent-lifecycle span operations in the GenAI conventions?
flashcards.a: create_agent, invoke_agent (the run-level span), and execute_tool (a tool-call child span).

flashcards.q: Name four key gen_ai.* attributes and what each carries.
flashcards.a: gen_ai.system (provider name), gen_ai.request.model / gen_ai.response.model (requested vs actually-served model), gen_ai.usage.input_tokens (cached+uncached combined), gen_ai.usage.output_tokens (completion tokens).

flashcards.q: Why does the convention store prompt/completion content in span events instead of span attributes?
flashcards.a: Attributes are indexed (expensive at scale), size-limited (full conversations often exceed caps), and exposed by default under a backend's retention policy, which is usually looser than the primary data store's -- a PII/compliance risk. Events avoid these constraints and are opt-in.

flashcards.q: What environment variable controls GenAI message content capture, and what's the default?
What are the three content-handling patterns the GenAI conventions document?
flashcards.a: Don't record content at all, record it directly as span events, or store it externally in a blob store and record only a reference/pointer in the span.

flashcards.q: What is the correct span hierarchy for a multi-step agent run?
flashcards.a: Run span (invoke_agent) contains step spans (one per loop iteration), each step span contains model spans (chat {provider}) and tool spans (execute_tool) as children; reasoning goes on the step span as an event.

flashcards.q: Why is head-based sampling the wrong default for GenAI traces?
flashcards.a: It decides to keep a trace probabilistically before the outcome is known, so it discards rare, expensive, or erroring traces at the same rate as routine ones -- exactly the traces worth keeping for incident review.

flashcards.q: Describe the standard tail-based sampling policy for GenAI traces.
flashcards.a: Keep 100% of traces with errors, 100% of traces over a cost threshold (e.g. $0.50/request), and sample the remaining routine traffic at 5-20%.

flashcards.q: Why is putting conversation_id or request_id on a metric label dangerous, even though it's fine on a span attribute?
flashcards.a: Metric backends create a new time series per unique label value; an unbounded ID value creates unbounded time series (cardinality explosion), inflating cost and degrading query performance. Traces don't pre-aggregate into per-dimension series the same way, so span/trace attributes are safe.

flashcards.q: Why shouldn't you hardcode a per-token dollar price into span-emission code?
flashcards.a: Provider prices change over time; a hardcoded price goes stale silently and can't represent historical pricing correctly. Emit raw token counts and compute cost downstream against a versioned, updatable price table.

flashcards.q: What is the join key for linking a production trace to an eval score and a cost figure?
flashcards.a: The trace_id -- an eval harness or online evaluator stores its result keyed by the trace ID that produced it, so a regression investigation can pull the exact trace directly.

flashcards.q: What does a trace showing only start/end timestamps and token counts fail to answer, and what fixes it?
flashcards.a: It can show THAT a run failed but not WHY -- fixing it requires step-level reasoning events and tool argument/result events, not just span timing.

flashcards.q: When is the full run/step/tool/model span hierarchy overkill?
flashcards.a: For a single-call feature with one prompt in, one completion out, no tool loop, and no multi-turn reasoning -- a single span with gen_ai.* attributes is sufficient there.
